papers.citation: Gottman, Swanson & Murray (1999). The mathematics of marital conflict: Dynamic mathematical nonlinear modeling of newlywed marital interaction. Journal of Family Psychology 13(1):3-19

Gottman, Levenson, Swanson, Swanson, Tyson & Yoshimoto (2003). Observing gay, lesbian and heterosexual couples' relationships: Mathematical modeling of conflict interaction. Journal of Homosexuality 45(1):65-91

experiment: Computational reproduction of the dyadic affect model: structural steady-state counts (E1), published-parameter consistency (E2), estimation-method recovery (E3), repair/damping (E4). No couple data; the model is imported from regesh/bonding/dyad.py and not re-implemented.
threshold_mapping: A spouse's published thresholds are those of the partner's response to that spouse: the husband's thresholds parameterize I_hw(H) in the wife's equation, the wife's thresholds parameterize I_wh(W) in the husband's equation (1999 Results: the husband's negative threshold is how negative he must become before his wife responds).
autoregressive_constant: a = u (1 - r) from the published inertia r and uninfluenced steady state u = a/(1 - r)

published_2003.claim: damping may create a positive-positive stable steady state (attractor) where none existed before

e1_structural.claim: for the sigmoidal influence function, we can have one, three, or five steady states; in most of our data there was only one influenced steady state per couple
e1_structural.plateau_convention: same (negative magnitude, positive magnitude) pair for both spouses; negative plateau is minus the magnitude; the subset with negative magnitude >= positive magnitude is tabulated separately
e1_structural.thresholds_source: Table 1 stable-group means (husband's thresholds for I_hw, wife's for I_wh); non-integer values avoid fixed points landing exactly on a jump of the step map
e1_structural.step_form: inertia crossed between spouses (9 pairs) x 49 uninfluenced pairs x 16 plateau pairs = 7056 couples; strict fixed points from steady_states() plus jump crossings of the completed null clines
e1_structural.smooth_form: sigmoid_ojive with shared inertia (3 values) x 25 uninfluenced pairs x 16 plateau pairs at width 1.0 (1200 couples); widths 0.5 and 2.0 at inertia 0.4 on the coarse uninfluenced grid {-3, 0, 3} (288 couples)

numeric_fixed_points.rationale: fixed_points_numeric with a 25x25 seed grid costs ~0.3 s per couple unloaded; the union of two offset coarse grids agreed with it on 150/150 pilot couples while a single 9x9 grid disagreed on 4/150. A declared random subsample is rechecked against the dense grid.

e2_published.influence_form: ojive (step), thresholds from the group means, plateau pair shared by both spouses
e2_published.match_norm: max over the two coordinates of the absolute difference between a model fixed point and the published (wife, husband) influenced steady-state means
e2_published.basin_classification: final state after 150 iterations: negative if both coordinates < 0, positive if both > 0, otherwise mixed; nearest fixed point also recorded

e3_recovery.noise_model: independent Gaussian process noise added to both equations at every step; the sum is rounded to the nearest integer (Python round, half to even) and clipped to the SPAFF range; the rounded clipped value is the state that propagates
e3_recovery.threshold_grid_rationale: for integer-valued series, a half-integer threshold selects the same subset as the adjacent integer under the <= / >= comparisons, so the module's default 0.5 grid adds only duplicates
e3_recovery.comparison_estimators: fit_joint_bilinear on all points (all noise levels); RecursiveIdentifier run online over the same series (primary noise level); both fit a bilinear partner equation, so only inertia and uninfluenced steady state are compared

e4_repair_damping.influence_form: bilinear (2003 preferred form), slopes shared by both spouses
e4_repair_damping.quadrant_rule: sign of (wife, husband) coordinates of each stable fixed point; a coordinate equal to zero counts as negative

workers_note: process pool size only; every task derives its seeds from indices and results are ordered, so outputs do not depend on the pool size
declared_ambiguities: The ojive plateau values (the fixed influence outside the thresholds) are not published for any group; they are swept (E2) or declared (E1, E3).
Threshold mapping: the husband's published thresholds are taken to parameterize the husband's influence on the wife, I_hw(H), following the 1999 Results text; the opposite mapping is not run.

Published Table 1 and Table 2 values are group means of per-couple estimates. A couple built from mean parameters need not have the mean influenced steady state, so an exact match in E2 is not expected and is not a reproduction criterion.

Within-paper inconsistency: the 1999 Results prose gives husbands' influenced steady states as -1.89 (divorced) and 0.72 (stable), which equal the uninfluenced means in Table 1; Table 1 lists -1.49 and 0.71. Table values are used.

The 1999 paper calls its form 'O-Jive or sigmoidal' and draws it as a step (Figure 1A). Both readings are run: the step map (exact piecewise-linear solver) and a logistic ramp of declared width centred on the thresholds (numeric solver). The ramp shape and widths are not from the paper.

For the step map the paper's graphical unstable steady states are crossings at the jumps of the null clines; they are not fixed points of the map. They are counted separately as jump crossings of the completed null clines.

Repair and damping are implemented as constant triggers (a jump of amplitude E once the partner's score crosses K), following the 2003 verbal description; the algorithmic details are in Gottman, Murray, Swanson, Tyson & Swanson (2002), which was not consulted. A reading of damping as a slope reduction is not implemented.
The damping threshold is not published; +6 is declared with sensitivities +4 and +8. Repair and damping terms are applied identically to both spouses because only group means are available.
Bilinear slopes are not published numerically in 2003 (only slope differences); 0.5/0.3 is declared with sensitivities.
E3's noise model, initial conditions, rounding and clipping are declared simulation choices; the papers analyse observed series and do not specify a generative noise model.
E3's integer threshold grid for the ojive fit is a declared choice; the papers do not state the grid used by the original program.
E2 theoretical conversations iterate the equations without clipping, as the papers describe; clipping would change basins.
The 2003 claim about damping refers to per-couple fitted models that are not available; E4 tests it on 1999 group-mean couples with 2003 group-mean repair/damping terms.

The smooth-form grid is coarser than the step-form grid (uninfluenced steps of 1.5 at width 1.0; {-3, 0, 3} for the width sensitivities at inertia 0.4) because the numeric fixed-point finder is about 400 times slower than the exact solver on the shared CPU.

Fixed points lying exactly on a jump of the step map are excluded by the module; non-integer published thresholds avoid such coincidences on the integer grids, and any remaining coincidence is flagged.
